summary: Wood enclosed lookout tower on Ball Mountain in the Klamath National Forest; a lookout since 1922 or earlier, rebuilt in 1940, and used for 2024 wildfire cameras.

facts.design: BC-301 cabin atop a 30-foot enclosed timber tower
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Register says a lookout existed on the site from 1922 or earlier; June 29, 1922 item has Jack Hayes taking up duties on Goose Nest mountain
October 4, 1923 item: Jack Hayes at the Ball Mountain station; the station was closed for the winter season
July 5, 1928 forest history entry: James Dysert listed to man the lookout in emergencies
July 10, 1935: Ranger Kreischer surveyed the Ball Mountain Lookout site (Shasta Forest); old tower on leased land
Shasta Forest bought the section for $500; deed dated September 26, 1936

Open platform tower with BC-201 cabin replaced by a BC-301 cabin on a 30-foot enclosed timber tower; October 3, 1940 CCC camp report says the new tower was well along and expected to be 75 percent complete before the winter shutdown
1952 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: lookout house is 14 feet square and about 25 feet high
October 31, 1960 recollection: box-like structure some 60 feet tall, with a Jacob's ladder as the fire escape
Forest Service decision signed June 28, 2024 for two wildfire cameras and a solar array on the communications tower at Ball Mountain; project status completed

corrections.why: The register and the 1940 report both give a 30-foot tower (9.1 m). The record's 4.3 m (14 feet) appears to be the 14-foot width of the lookout house in the 1952 survey description, not the height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1960 recollection says some 60 feet; the register and the 1940 report say 30 feet. The story uses 30 feet.

A June 1922 item places Jack Hayes on Goose Nest mountain; an October 1923 item places him at the Ball Mountain station. The story follows the 1923 item for the station name and reports the 1922 wording.
The 1940 tower is the current structure; the site had a lookout from 1922 or earlier, per the register.

notes_for_editor: Record height 4.3 m is most likely the 14-foot width of the lookout house (1952 station description: 14 ft square), not the height; the register and 1940 report say 30 feet and a 1960 recollection says about 60. The 2024 Forest Service project concerns a communications tower at Ball Mountain in the same section; the sources do not confirm that it is the historic lookout or whether the historic cabin stands. The Forest Lookouts page gives the township as 46N in its header but T45N in an author's note; the Forest Service project says T46N. The 1922 item names Goose Nest mountain. A separate Ball Mtn lookout sign (Mendocino NF, about 1940) was not used. The register's June 2025 photo was not added as a new find.
